body:
this is the current era as it sits on the site right now: showgirl, twelve songs in the track guide, four theories, four videos, and a timeline you can drag with your thumb.

the newest thing on it is dated august 11.

andrew lloyd webber — the cats and phantom composer, and one of the most serious private collectors of pre-raphaelite painting anywhere — posted a short video saying he had been listening to the album. "the track that really intrigues me is ‘the fate of ophelia.’"

he owns a version of the millais painting the whole era’s imagery keeps circling. it hangs, he said, in the room where they once had lunch. "so maybe she did."

he put no more weight on it than that maybe. neither will we.

why: SUBJECT SUBSTITUTED, and here is why. The calendar’s 08-15 23:00Z IG slot is an era-deep-cut on reputation with "vetted Vault photo with credit — era tile explicitly not acceptable here". No reputation photo exists in the #1903 library, /eras/reputation.png is inside the last-10 posted Instagram window (posted 2026-08-07) so the checker would reject it, and this PR is queue-only so it cannot commit a new capture. Rather than drop an Instagram day, the slot runs the strongest rung-1 asset the library does have — the real TLOAS era screenshot — with the same pillar and hook ("the artifact"). Everything in the caption is read off that screenshot (CURRENT ERA, 12-song track guide, 4 theories & eggs, 4 videos, the draggable timeline, the August 11, 2026 moment at the top of the feed) or traced to the Vault TLOAS item "Andrew Lloyd Webber hears his own Ophelia in ‘The Fate of Ophelia’" (2026-08-11, sourced Yahoo Creators + his own Instagram + WHYY): his Pre-Raphaelite collection, the "the track that really intrigues me" quote, and the carefully-hedged "maybe she did" about the Millais version in his house. The caption keeps his hedge intact instead of upgrading it to influence — the Vault says the Millais parallel was never confirmed by Taylor or her photographers, and this post says so. DEPLOY DEPENDENCY: needs #1903 deployed.
